equity_bridge.item: Work-off of excess customer advances (contract liabilities 158.5 vs ~50 normal, at ~92% cost)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 AR note 12 line 6829; DeferredRevenue kpi FY2019-25 range 12.5-61.3

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR (FY2027 guided 'flattish', FY2028-30 contract ramp, then GDP-plus fade); equity 5yr CAGR 7.5% overstated by the 85% payout being retained in cash rather than reinvested, and the FY2023-26 revenue/EPS CAGRs describe a two-year 50% expansion management itself says is over
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 9.1% vs revenue 17.5% and EPS 31.9%: divergence >30% - the FY2024-26 step-up is a cycle peak (revenue +31.5% FY2026, guided flat FY2027), not a compounding base. Owner-FCF CAGRs (46.8%/64.4%) are dominated by working-capital swings (FY2021 owner FCF $15.6m, FY2026 $187.2m of which ~$73m WC) and are not used.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs computed on owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income (FY2021 15.6, FY2023 59.2, FY2026 187.2). SBC has grown from 0.14% to 0.36% of revenue since FY2021 but remains immaterial; the divergence between owner and reported FCF CAGRs is interest income (0.4 -> 9.3), not SBC.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 is the consolidation year management guided (+2%), followed by a three-year ramp (+7/+6/+5%) as the record FY2026 order intake and the $680m+ secured since 1 July 2026 convert to revenue in FY2028+, fading to 2.5% by year 10. The EBITDA margin drifts from the 8.1% FY2026 record back to a 7.25% mid-cycle level - the IFRS-16-equivalent ten-year mean - because the FY2025-26 expansion (6.3% -> 8.1%) was operating leverage on a 50% revenue step-up that is now over. Leases and hire purchase are charged as an operating cost (~1.1% of revenue), owned-PPE capex settles at 1.25%, working capital consumes 5.5c per dollar of growth, cash tax 30%.
scenario_narratives.bull: FY2027 delivers the modest-growth end of guidance (+5%) and FY2028-29 compound at +12/+10% as electrification, BESS/wind (Zenviron), gas construction and copper/critical-minerals processing come on top of sustained Pilbara maintenance; the Kerman/APIP/High Energy Service acquisitions widen the addressable market. Margin holds at ~8% on scale and maintenance mix. Ten-year revenue CAGR ~6%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Iron ore and energy capex roll over in FY2027-28: awards are deferred, shutdown scopes shrink, and competitive tendering compresses the margin to the 6.2% that prevailed through FY2020-24. Revenue retraces ~14% before resuming low growth. The net-cash balance sheet means no distress, but the valuation carries no re-rating and the terminal cap (14x) binds on a smaller FCF base.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A capital-light, net-cash, 85%-payout contractor whose value is a mid-cycle owner-FCF stream, not the FY2026 peak. Three deliberate choices drive the result: (1) the FCF base is normalised for a $73m working-capital inflow and the $105m of excess customer advances is worked off in the bridge; (2) margins mean-revert toward the ten-year IFRS-16-equivalent average rather than holding the record; (3) risk is charged once - a single 10% AUD WACC, with cyclicality in the bear path and a 25% bear weight - and the terminal value is capped at 14x FCF because the market has historically paid ~8-12x EBITDA for this business.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: every 0.5pp of sustained EBITDA margin is worth roughly $2/share; if the FY2026 8.1% proves structural (maintenance mix, scale), the base is too low
Working-capital normalisation: if elevated customer advances persist across the contract book rather than unwinding, the $95m bridge deduction is too harsh (~$0.94/share)
Terminal multiple: the market currently pays ~25x FY2026 earnings and ~13x EV/EBITDA; the 14x FCF cap embeds no re-rating and the price implies the market disagrees
Cycle timing: the bear path assumes a 2027-28 downturn; a longer resources capex cycle (energy transition metals, gas, data-centre power) shifts weight to bull
Revenue definition: statutory revenue (2,796) excludes the $193m JV share; JV profits are inside EBITDA but only their dividends are cash

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report, cash-flow reconciliation 'Share-based payment expense' 10,063 ($'000, line 6362); equity-award taxes nil (no net-share settlement, rights vest gross)
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average from the FY2026 EPS note (99.795m basic + 1.168m dilutive rights = 100.963m). Shares on issue at the report date ~100.5m (final dividend $59.3m / 59c) plus 1.35m unvested performance rights; held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). DRP adds ~0.13m shares/yr ($4.05m reinvested FY2026) - immaterial, not modelled.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: 10-yr ACGB ~4.4%, ERP 5.5%, beta ~1.05 for an ASX200 mining/energy-services contractor -> cost of equity ~10.2%; no interest-bearing debt so WACC = cost of equity, rounded to 10.0%. One WACC for all three scenarios: cyclicality, customer concentration and the FY27 consolidation year are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations (f)).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. Full lease + hire-purchase cash cost (principal $24.1m financing line 5747/kpis LeasePrincipalRepayment + finance costs paid $3.5m line 5723 = $27.7m, 0.99% of revenue) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities ($72.0m, incl. hire purchase) are EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (owned PPE 26.8 + amortisation 2.0 = $28.9m, 1.03% of revenue; ROU depreciation 8.3 + HP 9.8 excluded) so the lease is not charged twice in taxable EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: None required: NCI nil at 30 June 2026 (line 5513). Zenviron and other JVs are equity-accounted; their profit share ($16.0m) sits inside reported EBITDA and their dividends ($7.3m) in OCF - the margin paths are set below the FY2026 print partly for this non-cash gap.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' + adaptations file: AUD WACC, leases treatment B, SBC-light market). Revenue base is STATUTORY revenue 2,796.1 (contracts with customers 2,786.8 + other 9.3), not the $2,980m 'revenue including joint ventures' headline (which adds a $193.3m JV share, page 17 reconciliation); EBITDA margins are therefore expressed on the statutory base (FY2026 226.0/2796.1 = 8.08%, or 7.75% after stripping the $9.3m interest income that is deducted separately). FCF BASE IS NOT FY2026 AS PRINTED: FY2026 OCF $245.1m carried a +$72.9m net working-capital inflow (payables +110.3, provisions +33.0, receivables -60.9; contract liabilities tripled 53.2 -> 158.5). OCF ex-WC was ~$172m; normalised owner FCF (ex-WC, less capex 38.5, SBC 10.1, interest income 9.3, lease cash 27.7) is ~$87m, and the component build's FY2027 base-case owner FCF (~$85-90m) ties to that, not to the $187m last_fcf. The excess customer advances (~$105m above the FY2019-25 norm of ~$50m) are cash already in the $293.6m pile that will be worked off at cost, so the equity bridge deducts $95m (105 x ~92% cost ratio). Interest income stripped because net cash $293.6m > 1x the FCF base. Buybacks: none in ten years; the flat count is a modelling convention funded by full SBC expensing, not by repurchases. Non-cash hire-purchase asset additions ($19.6m FY2026) are paid for through the lease line, so capex_pct covers owned PPE only. Cash tax at the 30% Australian statutory rate (FY2026 paid $62.9m = 35% of PBT, a catch-up on FY2025's $39.1m; expense 29.2%).
inputs.working_capital_note: Net operating working capital (receivables 554.9 + contract assets 21.7 - payables incl. contract liabilities 419.9) = $156.7m = 5.6% of revenue; growth CONSUMES cash, so wc_capture_pct is -5.5 (contractor sign, adaptations checklist). FY2026's positive swing was contract-liability timing, handled once in the equity bridge.

bear.narrative: A commodity downturn (iron ore ~26% and WA ~68% of revenue) defers construction awards and thins shutdown scopes: revenue falls ~14% over FY2027-29 to ~$2.4bn (still above FY2025) and the margin reverts to the FY2020-24 ~6.2% level as fixed-price tender competition and labour inflation bite. Balance sheet holds; this is an earnings path, not a solvency one.

base.narrative: FY2027 flat-to-modest per guidance, FY2028-30 ramp as the ~$2.7bn of FY2026 awards and $680m+ of early-FY2027 awards phase in, then fade to GDP-plus. EBITDA margin reverts from the 8.1% FY2026 peak toward the 7.25% IFRS-16-equivalent ten-year mean (post-IFRS-16 FY2020-25 range 6.1-7.3%; FY2016-19 8.1-9.5% on a like-for-like basis).

bull.narrative: The 'modest growth' end of FY2027 guidance lands, then the energy-transition/electrification pipeline (Zenviron BESS and wind, High Energy Service HV work, gas construction, copper/critical-minerals processing) compounds on top of Pilbara sustaining and maintenance volumes for a second multi-year expansion. Operating leverage holds the margin at ~8% rather than reverting.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: revenue is geared to customer commodity capex the company does not control, iron ore ~26% and WA ~68% of revenue, and management has already guided a flat year at the top of the cycle. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs both a second expansion leg AND margin held at the cycle peak, two independent conditions. Base 50%: guidance-anchored and mid-cycle.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
